requirements.requirement: Restore every invoice named in restore-request.txt into live/ with the archived bytes and file modes.
requirements.summary: The request names INV-100.txt and INV-101.txt. Both exist after restoration and after restart; each live SHA-256 equals its archive SHA-256, and each mode is 0644, matching the archive inventory.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the current customers.csv contents and do not restore unrelated archived files.
requirements.summary: customers.csv retains the preparation-baseline SHA-256. The final live inventory contains exactly customers.csv and the two requested invoices; archived old-notes.txt and the archived customer register were not restored.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic are directly observed before and after the work and restart. The restoration used the platform's existing shell, tar, and standard utilities; no package or platform change is evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre/post and archive-to-live verification. The requested invoices were selectively restored with correct bytes and modes, the newer customer register remained unchanged, unrelated archive entries were excluded, and the legacy OS/kernel were retained. The mandatory restart protocol also demonstrates persistence and recovery.
limitations: Systemd failed-unit observation was unsupported on this legacy platform; no task service or cluster was involved, and SSH recovery plus post-restart data and platform checks provide the applicable recovery evidence.
Requirement preserve-and-select cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were observed. The selective extraction was the required task mutation (cmd-d2bcbe9d665f4ae2). The scheduled reboot and temporary log redirection were required for provider-wide restart evidence (cmd-83cf9217e48d40e3); the post-run /tmp inventory is empty, so no residue remained. All other commands were read-only discovery, verification, or restart polling. Restart evidence is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart data and boot ID, acknowledgement, bounded unavailability, a different post-restart boot ID, and recovered data/platform state; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree.
